bounds.derivation: Draw the initial vector $g_0\sim\mathcal N(0,I_d)$. With probability at least $1-\delta$, both $|u_1^{\mathsf T}g_0|\ge c\delta$ and $\|g_0\|_2\le C\sqrt{d/\delta}$ hold. Choose a scaled Chebyshev polynomial $P_t$ of degree at most $t$ such that $P_t(\lambda_1)=1$ and $\max_{x\in[0,\lambda_2]}|P_t(x)|\le2\exp(-ct\sqrt\gamma)$; if $\lambda_2=0$, one matrix application suffices. The vector $P_t(A)g_0$ lies in the Krylov subspace, and the sine of its angle to $u_1$ is at most $C\sqrt d\,\delta^{-3/2}\exp(-ct\sqrt\gamma)$. The unit vector maximizing the Rayleigh quotient in that subspace has no greater Rayleigh loss. By $\lambda_1-\lambda_2\ge\gamma\lambda_1$, dividing the normalized Rayleigh loss by $\gamma$ bounds the squared sine error. Thus $t=O\!\bigl(\gamma^{-1/2}\log(Cd/(\delta\varepsilon\gamma))\bigr)$ suffices. The unknown values $\lambda_1,\lambda_2$ are used only to prove the existence of the polynomial; the algorithm need not know them. The projected matrix is formed from the queried Krylov vectors. Alternatively, $d$ standard-basis queries reconstruct the matrix exactly.

bounds.derivation: Use the rank-one hard instance from Theorem 2.2 of Simchowitz, El Alaoui, and Recht (2018). Set its asymptotic relative gap to $h=7\gamma\le1/2$ and choose $\lambda>1$ so that $s=\lambda+\lambda^{-1}=2/(1-h)$. The source matrix is $M=W+\lambda u_0u_0^{\mathsf T}$, where $W$ is its normalized Gaussian symmetric noise matrix and $u_0$ is the hidden unit vector. On the source event $E_{\mathrm{good}}(1/2)$, we have $\lambda_1(M)\le3s/2$ and $\lambda_1(M)-\|W\|_{\mathrm{op}}\ge(s-2)/2=hs/2$, hence $\|W\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le s+1$. Setting $B=M+2sI_d$ gives $B\succ0$, $\lambda_1(B)\le7s/2$, and relative leading-eigenvalue gap at least $h/7=\gamma$. Then $A=(2\Lambda/(7s))B$ ensures $\lambda_1(A)\le\Lambda$. The matrices $A$ and $M$ have the same leading eigenvector; each $A$ product is simulated by exactly one $M$ query and public linear operations. If the squared sine error is at most $\varepsilon^2\le h/12$, the output has Rayleigh quotient for $|M|=(M^2)^{1/2}$ at least $(1-h/12)\|M\|_{\mathrm{op}}$, meeting the source theorem's target. The theorem therefore excludes unrestricted randomized adaptive algorithms using fewer than $ch^{-1/2}\log d$ queries. The sufficient dimension threshold $D_0(\gamma)$ retains the polynomial conditions in Proposition 2.1 and Theorem 6.1 and the condition making the failure bound a constant; unspecified constants remain unspecified. In the region $\delta=1/10$, $\gamma^2\le\varepsilon^2\le\gamma/12$, and $d\ge\max\{D_0(\gamma),\gamma^{-2}\}$, all additional upper-bound logarithms are controlled by $\log d$, giving $\Theta(\gamma^{-1/2}\log d)$.

evidence.supports: An arbitrary-randomized adaptive PCA lower bound transfers through explicit affine shifting, scaling, and angle conversion to the PSD bound $\Omega(\gamma^{-1/2}\log d)$.
notes: Use the rank-one hard instance from Theorem 2.2 of Simchowitz, El Alaoui, and Recht (2018). Set its asymptotic relative gap to $h=7\gamma\le1/2$ and choose $\lambda>1$ so that $s=\lambda+\lambda^{-1}=2/(1-h)$. The source matrix is $M=W+\lambda uu^{\mathsf T}$, where $W$ is its normalized Gaussian symmetric noise matrix and $u$ is the hidden unit vector. On the source event $E_{\mathrm{good}}(1/2)$, we have $\lambda_1(M)\le3s/2$ and $\lambda_1(M)-\|W\|_{\mathrm{op}}\ge(s-2)/2=hs/2$, hence $\|W\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le s+1$. The theorem therefore excludes unrestricted randomized adaptive algorithms using fewer than $ch^{-1/2}\log d$ queries. The sufficient dimension threshold $D_0(\gamma)$ retains the polynomial conditions in Proposition 2.1 and Theorem 6.1 and the condition making the failure bound a constant; unspecified constants remain unspecified. In the region $\delta=1/10$, $\gamma^2\le\varepsilon^2\le\gamma/12$, and $d\ge\max\{D_0(\gamma),\gamma^{-2}\}$, all additional upper-bound logarithms are controlled by $\log d$, giving $\Theta(\gamma^{-1/2}\log d)$.
